name: passenger_car_225_45r17
source: Plausible Magic Formula (MF5.2) coefficient magnitudes for a mid-size performance passenger tyre, following the coefficient naming and equation structure of Pacejka, 'Tyre and Vehicle Dynamics', 3rd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 2012), ch. 4. NOT a measured/proprietary .tir for a specific commercial tyre - PLAN.md P3 explicitly allows 'published or plausible' data with the source noted. Peak friction coefficients (Dx1/Dy1 ~= 1.0-1.05) and cornering/longitudinal stiffness magnitudes (Kx/Ky ~= 16-18x Fz) are consistent with the typical ranges Pacejka's own Table 4.2 and Milliken, 'Race Car Vehicle Dynamics' (SAE, 1995) ch. 2 cite for radial passenger/performance tyres. Dimensions (unloaded_radius=0.317 m, width=0.205 m) match a 225/45R17 tyre's nominal geometry and data/models/car_sedan/car_sedan.rig.json's own wheel radius. low_speed_damping_ratio/low_speed_damping_vx (PHYS-033 I1) were chosen by measurement against the standstill-wiggle telemetry (CLAUDE.md's Vehicle system section), not from a published tyre. PHYS-036 (2026-09-24): the 'aligning' block's qdz1/qdz2 sign was flipped (was +0.10/-0.02) - Pacejka's own convention is Mz0 = -t*Fy0 with pneumatic trail t > 0 (ch. 4, eq. 4.E70 family), i.e. Dz and Dy must carry OPPOSITE signs so Mz0 opposes (not reinforces) Fy0; the shipped value had the same sign as Dy, steering the car further into a turn instead of resisting. qbz1 was raised from 8.0 to 43.4 (same Bx-scaling technique Pacejka's own B/C/D/E family uses: the curve's shape is a function of B*alpha alone at fixed C/D/E, so scaling B alone rescales the peak's alpha location without touching its height) so the curve peaks at ~4 deg of slip instead of ~21.7 deg - real passenger-tyre self-aligning-torque curves peak in roughly the 2-6 deg range, well before the ~9 deg Fy0 peak at fz0 (Pacejka ch. 4; Milliken ch. 2's qualitative trail-vs-slip-angle curves). qcz1/qez1 (curve shape) are unchanged; this model's own single-curve Mz0(alpha) simplification (this project's pacejka_tyre_model.cpp header comment) does not reproduce a real tyre's return to near-zero Mz at very large slip (it plateaus near its peak magnitude instead, an accepted limitation of the simplified shape - see test_pacejka_tyre_model.cpp). Longitudinal shape refit (2026-09-25, owner report 'a lot of wheel spin in 2nd'): pcx1 1.65 -> 1.42 and pex1 0.10 -> -0.45; pdx*/pkx* (peak Dx, slip stiffness Kx) unchanged. The old C put the Fx0 large-slip asymptote at sin(C*pi/2) = 0.52 of peak (Fx(kappa=1)/peak 0.66, Fx(kappa=3)/peak 0.57), so a tyre pushed past its peak lost a third to almost half its drive and could never pull itself back - far below the measured locked-wheel/peak ratio of a dry-asphalt passenger tyre (Wong, 'Theory of Ground Vehicles' 5th ed., Table 1.3: mu_peak 0.8-0.9, mu_slide 0.75, i.e. ~0.85-0.9 of peak). C=1.42 moves the asymptote to 0.79; E=-0.45 (E<0 steepens the approach to it, as this file's own lateral block already does with pcy1 1.35/pey1 -0.6) keeps the peak slip where it was. Result at fz0 (and 0.75*fz0): peak slip 0.141 (0.146), Fx(kappa=0.5)/peak 0.884, Fx(kappa=1)/peak 0.839 (0.841), Fx(kappa=3)/peak 0.807 (0.807); the pre-peak curve moves by < 0.012*Fz. Combined-slip rbx*/rcx*/rby*/rcy* unchanged (they shape the cross-slip weighting, not the pure-slip asymptote; the max combined resultant over kappa 0..3 x alpha 0..0.3 is 1.071*Fz before and after). Pinned by tests/unit/test_pacejka_tyre_model.cpp's 'longitudinal slide-to-peak ratios' case. Rolling resistance (2026-10-06, tyre crr work): qsy1/qsy3/qsy4 are now DERIVED from the rolling_resistance anchor block - crr = crr_base*(1 + A*(v/V_r) + B*(v/V_r)^4) with crr(0.8 V_r) = 1.5 crr_base and crr(V_r) = 2.0 crr_base [AS: the 1.5/2.0 rise anchors sit between the Gillespie and Wong passenger-tyre forms, neither re-checked against a readable source], rated speed V_r [C] ISO 4000-1 / ETRTO speed symbol W = 270 km/h (quoted from memory of the symbol table, not re-read this session); replaces the raw qsy4 0.0002*(v/16.7)^4 (tractor 0.0003*(v/8.3)^4) which cost 30x the base at 370 km/h on the hypercar.
